decisions.reason: The second V height and visual-role refinement does not change the construction rules for the other proprietary letterforms; their separate same-message clarification is already represented.
The É accent remains the fixed upper reference for the second V hierarchy; its derivation, geometry, and peak alignment are unchanged.
The source changes only the supporting second V's relative height and prominence, not the approved Hero V geometry or role.
The complete-wordmark composition remains valid unchanged; the refined skyline relationship and quiet role are owned by the atomic second V Requirement and should not be duplicated here.
The source does not change the shared terminal gesture or its application; it changes only the second V's height hierarchy and visual prominence.
The second V hierarchy refinement has no necessary effect on the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
The broad brand-expression principles remain unchanged; the quiet architectural-echo instruction is a concrete second V treatment rather than a new brand-level rule.
The identity remains wordmark-led without a separate icon or monogram; the second V refinement does not alter that architecture.
The second V design refinement does not change the production-ready asset deliverable.
